The single most important thing to know about this word is that "domestic" always points to some kind of home. That one idea is the thread connecting all its meanings — and once you hold onto it, everything else makes sense.
Meaning 1: Of or relating to the home and household life

This is the most direct meaning. When "domestic" describes things that belong to, happen inside, or are connected with a home and family, it carries this sense.

  • Domestic chores — tasks done around the house: cooking, cleaning, doing laundry
  • Domestic life — the everyday rhythm of living at home with family
  • Domestic appliances — machines used in the home: a refrigerator, a washing machine, a microwave
  • Domestic violence / domestic abuse — harm that takes place within a home, usually between partners, spouses, or family members
  • Domestic bliss — a phrase used (sometimes sarcastically) to describe a happy, peaceful home life

In all these cases, the word simply signals: this belongs to the home and the private life of a family.
Meaning 2: Of or relating to one's own country, as opposed to another country

A country can be thought of as a collective "home" — the place a nation belongs to. When "domestic" is used this way, it always contrasts with words like foreign, international, or overseas.

  • Domestic flights — flights within the same country (Delhi to Mumbai), as opposed to international flights
  • Domestic policy — decisions and rules a government makes for people within its own country (not for other countries)
  • Domestic market — buyers, sellers, and businesses operating inside a country
  • Domestic terrorism — acts of political violence carried out by citizens or residents against their own country, from within its borders
  • Domestic beer / wine — alcohol produced inside the country, not imported

You'll also come across the famous phrase Gross Domestic Product (GDP) — the total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders. The word "domestic" there is doing exactly this job: marking something as belonging to one's own national territory.

Whenever you see "domestic" used this way, it is drawing a line between here (our country) and out there (other countries).
Meaning 3: Describing animals (or plants) tamed and integrated into human life

Certain animals have been living alongside humans for thousands of years — bred, raised, and cared for by people. These are called domestic animals (or domesticated animals). The opposite is wild.

  • Domestic animals: dogs, cats, cattle, horses, goats, chickens — animals that live under human care and depend on it
  • A domestic dog is the tame companion animal; a wolf is its wild counterpart
  • A domestic cat lives in your house; a wild cat or feral cat does not

The idea is the same: the animal is "of the home" — it lives with humans rather than in the wild.
Meaning 4: A person who is inclined toward, comfortable with, or skilled at home life

Less commonly, "domestic" can describe a person's character or temperament when they are naturally suited to managing a home — cooking, maintaining a household, caring for family.

  • "She's very domestic — she loves baking and keeping the house in perfect order."
  • "He's not really the domestic type; he'd rather be outdoors."

This meaning is softer and more informal. It's not an insult, but it can sometimes carry outdated stereotypical connotations (e.g., implying a woman "belongs in the home"), so context matters when you encounter it.
The whole picture at a glance

Every meaning of "domestic" maps back to the idea of home:

SenseThe "home" being referred to
HouseholdThe physical home — rooms, routines, family
NationalThe country as a collective home
Animals/plantsThe human home as opposed to the wild
Personal characterA person's affinity for home life

"Domestic" never carries a positive or negative meaning on its own. Domestic life can be warm and comfortable. Domestic violence is deeply serious. Domestic policy is neutral and bureaucratic. Domestic animals are simply tamed. The word itself is factual and descriptive — its tone depends entirely on what it is paired with.

Once you remember that "domestic" = of the home — whether that home is a household, a country, or the human world as opposed to the wild — you have the full word. Every time you meet it, ask yourself: which kind of "home" is being talked about here? The answer will always tell you exactly what it means.
